$comment: The single source of truth for exercise identity across mova and Phoenix.
Python reads this file via src/mova_imu/exercises/ids.py.
TypeScript mirrors it in services/frontend/src/lib/exercises/ids.ts, and
src/lib/exercises/ids.test.ts reads THIS file and fails if the two drift.
Three id spaces exist and none of them can be derived from another by
string transformation. Guessing is exactly how 'heel-slide' and
'heel_slide' became two different things, so a missing row raises rather
than being computed.
catalog  kebab-case. services/frontend/src/lib/exercises/catalog.ts and
the public.exercises table. This is the canonical id: it is what
the hosted database holds and what every runtime path resolves.
scoring  snake_case. The ExerciseSlug union in lib/scoring/types.ts.
null when the exercise has no scoring config.
phoenix  Phoenix's exercise_signals.SIGNAL_PROFILES key, which is what the
vendored analysis in services/imu-tools is keyed on.
null when Phoenix has no signal profile for it.
This table maps IDENTITY ONLY. It never carries a threshold, a target or a
sensor list: those live in each system's own config, and the two do not
always agree. mova's catalog states a 20 deg total cycle and an 8 deg
minimum valid excursion for ankle-pumps, while Phoenix's profile uses
enter_deg 4.0 because it counts one direction of the pump only, with its
own comment saying that is unvalidated on hardware. Both are true of their
own system; neither may be copied into the other without a clinician.

$why: Phoenix signal profiles with no mova catalog entry. Listed explicitly so
tests/test_ids.py can assert that the table plus this list partitions
SIGNAL_PROFILES exactly -- a profile added upstream and forgotten here
fails a test instead of silently having no mova exercise.
Both of these are thigh-absolute-angle exercises that mova has no
clinician-recorded clip for. Held for a second pass rather than shipped
into the library with no reference footage.
